title: Rate mediator: Redis-lease failover + proportional shedding to preserve SLOs during limiter outages
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: When the primary distributed limiter (Redis-based lease allocator) experiences network partitions or sustained high latencies, customers see large, correlated 429 waves and rising p99 latency due to abrupt reject spikes. Existing fallback (stateless local tokens) is too aggressive and results in tenant unfairness and SLO violations for latency-sensitive routes.

Goal: Implement a 'rate mediator' that gracefully degrades limiter behavior during partial failures by combining fast local smoothing, proportional shedding (based on tenant SLO headroom), and an eventual fallback lease reconciliation to Redis. The mediator must limit blast radius, maintain proportional fairness between tenants, and prioritize low-latency routes to protect SLOs.

Scope: engineering work across runtime (fast path), global router, and console metrics. Deliverables: design doc, canary rollout, automated chaos tests, dashboards and alerting, implementation + integration tests, and rollout plan with rollback criteria.
acceptance_criteria: During simulated Redis high-latency outage, overall 429 rate across canary region does not exceed 4x baseline and tenant-level 429 distribution remains proportional to baseline allocations
p95/p99 latency for routes marked latency-sensitive increases no more than 15% under degraded conditions in chaos test
No additional tail latency introduced in normal operation (regression guarded by CI benchmarks)
Automated chaos scenarios (partition, slow Redis) pass end-to-end tests and metrics are recorded in controlled experiment logs
Console shows new dashboard tiles: limiter_headroom, proportional_shed_fraction, local_smooth_rate, reconciler_lag
technical_decisions: Use Redis leases as authoritative under healthy conditions; on detection of high Redis response time (>50ms median over 30s) the mediator switches to hybrid mode
Hybrid mode = local leaky-bucket with rate smoothing + proportional shedding computed from per-tenant SLO headroom (recent 5m error and latency budgets)
Proportional shedding uses soft-weights derived from 5m-weighted tenant usage rather than hard tokens to avoid starvation of low-volume tenants
Lease rehydration is performed asynchronously with backoff; reconciliation uses monotonic counters and idempotent apply to avoid double-counting grants
We will implement a bounded reservation queue for short bursts (200ms max hold) to absorb transient spikes without immediate shedding
Telemetry exposed via new metrics (see acceptance_criteria) with 10s granularity and tagging by tenant_id, region, route, and mode (normal|hybrid|degraded)
implementation_tasks: Spike: benchmark local leaky-bucket smoothing algorithm with production request traces (Aisha + Priya) — DONE
Design doc: runtime design + API changes for router to query mediator (Marco) — IN REVIEW https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/infra/Rate+Mediator
Implement mediator: local smoothing + proportional shed logic (Marco) — WIP branch github.com/redwood/inference/pull/5120
Integration: router fallback hook and canary flags (Sung)
Reconciler: async Redis lease rehydration with idempotent apply (Diego)
Unit + e2e tests including chaos scenarios (partition, slow response, redis restart) (QA)
Telemetry: add Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboard panels (Observability)
Load test: run 3 x baseline QPS spike tests with and without mediator; record fairness metrics per-tenant (DST)
qa_plan: Create synthetic multi-tenant traffic generator using production trace replay (10% of prod scale)
Run chaos: introduce Redis latency in steps (50ms, 100ms, 300ms) and verify mediator transitions and reconcilations
Assert metrics in Prometheus for headroom and shed fraction; compare to baseline stored in experiment dashboard
Validate no regression in steady-state latency by running CI micro-benchmarks against runtime-2.4 branch
rollout_plan: Phase 1: deploy mediator behind feature flag to staging; run 24h soak with synthetic traffic
Phase 2: Canary in 1 region (us-west-2) at 5% of traffic for 48h; monitor p95/p99, 429 rate, proportional fairness metric
Phase 3: Gradual ramp 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 3 days with automated pause on alert
Rollback: immediate disable feature flag and revert reconciler state if per-tenant p99 breach > 2x baseline or 429 spike > 8x baseline
Post-deploy: 7-day observation window with retention of detailed logs for reconciliation debugging
dashboards_and_alerting: New Grafana board: Rate Mediator Overview (panels for headroom, shed_fraction, local_smooth_rate, reconciler_lag)
Alerts: limiter_mediator_mode_change > 3 transitions in 5m => paging; proportional_shed_fraction > 0.5 for >10m => paged
SLO alert mapping: if latency-sensitive route p99 breaches > 10% above baseline for 10m, trigger rollback runbook
updates: 2026-01-18: Spike completed. Local smoothing reduced p99 amplification in 10/12 trace replays. Observed slight unfairness for <0.1% tenants under extreme bursts.
2026-01-22: Design doc posted for review. PM requested clearer operator runbook for rollback criteria.
2026-01-29: Prototype mediator merged behind flag; reconciler stubs added. Initial e2e harness failing under partition (race in lease rehydration). Assigned to Diego to fix idempotency edge-case.
2026-02-05: Diego fixed idempotent reconciler logic and added monotonic counter checks. Chaos test now transitions cleanly from normal->hybrid->reconciled in 95% of runs.
2026-02-12: Observability panels in draft; added tenant fairness metric (KL divergence vs baseline) to dashboard. Ready for canary planning.
2026-02-20: Canary flags created; scheduled canary starting 2026-02-24 in us-west-2 with 5% traffic. QA will run Redis latency experiments during canary window.
notes: Trade-offs considered: stronger local quotas would be simpler but would risk tenant starvation; chose proportional shed to preserve fairness at expense of slightly more complex reconciliation logic.
Long-term: consider moving leases to multi-master tag-based KV or replacing Redis with consensus-backed lease store to reduce single-component fragility.
Operator ergonomics: add a single 'mediator mode' toggle in Console plus per-customer override to opt-out during full-failover exercises.
